slides.punch: The target is 30× the run-rate IREN has actually delivered.
slides.why: This is the number that moves the stock: not quarterly revenue, but a year-end run-rate target. November: $3B. February: unchanged. May: raised to $4B. slides.src: 8-K EX-99.1, Q1 FY26 Consolidated Statement of Operations
slides.head: The ‘record’ quarter, walked line by line
slides.punch: 173% of the ‘record’ profit is a paper gain.
slides.why: Back in September, IREN reported net income of $385M — a record, and the headline everywhere. Walk it. Running the business that quarter actually lost $76.4M. Add a $665M unrealized gain — a paper markup on derivatives tied to its convertible notes, nothing to do with selling compute — and a little more from interest and FX, and the picture flips to $575M of income before tax. Subtract tax, and you get the record quarter. 173% of this company's only profitable quarter this year came from an accounting mark, not from a customer.
slides.notes: Finding two, and it explains the one quarter that looked great. Back in September, IREN reported net income of three hundred eighty-four million six — a record, and the headline everywhere. Walk it. Running the business that quarter actually lost seventy-six million four. Add back a six hundred sixty-five million dollar unrealized gain — a paper markup on derivatives tied to their convertible notes, nothing to do with operations — and the picture flips to five hundred seventy-five million of pretax income. Subtract tax, and you get your record quarter. Every dollar of this company's only profitable quarter came from an accounting mark, not from selling anything.

slides.punch: NVIDIA is betting on execution, not the stock price today.
slides.why: NVIDIA is not just selling IREN GPUs — it bought itself an option. The right to buy 30.0M IREN shares at $70.00 each, worth up to $2.1B if fully exercised. Read it as a signal, not a threat: NVIDIA structured its own money so it only pays off if the build-out actually happens.

The right to purchase thirty million IREN shares at seventy dollars each, worth up to two point one billion dollars if it is ever fully exercised. But it only vests as NVIDIA actually delivers GPUs — up to six hundred thousand of them — through May of twenty thirty-one. Seventy dollars is sixty-seven percent above where the stock trades today. Read it as a signal: NVIDIA is betting the stock gets there if the buildout works, and structured the deal so it only pays off if it actually does.

Stock up roughly 50% off its July low, on contract headlines with no financials attached
Total revenue and Adjusted EBITDA have fallen for two straight quarters
The only profitable quarter this year ran on a one-time derivative gain, not operations

scored.fact: $2.8B of new contracts since July; ARR target raised twice
Up ~50% off the July low on contract headlines alone
The 'record' quarter was a one-time gain
$520M more in impairments still to book

working: The demand is real and the counterparties are real: Microsoft, NVIDIA, and a widening customer list, with a 5-year, $9.7B Microsoft contract as the anchor.
IREN has a genuine track record of delivering data-center capacity on schedule — Horizon 1 was built and handed to Microsoft on the timeline management set.
NVIDIA is not just a customer — it is a $2.1B potential investor, vesting its right to buy shares only as IREN actually delivers GPUs. That aligns its incentives with execution, not promises.
The company is diversifying its funding — customer prepayments, GPU-specific financing and convertible notes — rather than relying on one source.
Every dollar of Bitcoin-mining capacity retired is capacity that can be re-let at AI Cloud pricing, which is why AI Cloud revenue has grown every single quarter even as total revenue fell.
watch: The Aug 27 earnings print has to show the AI Cloud ramp finally outrunning the Bitcoin-mining decline, or the two-quarter revenue slide becomes three.
The disclosed $520M of additional impairments has not been booked yet — expect it to land across the next few quarters and to keep pressuring GAAP net income.
NVIDIA's $70 strike is 68% above today's price — not a near-term dilution risk, but a marker of where NVIDIA itself expects the stock to trade if the buildout goes well.
IREN keeps issuing shares through its ATM program — 357.4 million shares outstanding as of Apr 30 2026, and rising — which dilutes every existing holder a little more with each raise.

Almost none of this stock's biggest moves this year have come from a quarterly earnings release — they have come from standalone contract-announcement press releases with no financial statements attached.
why: The demand is real. Microsoft, NVIDIA and a widening customer base are paying real money, and IREN has a track record of building on schedule.
The price already needs a lot to go right. At $41.63 the stock sits above my base case and inside my bull-case range — you are already paying for meaningful execution, not just potential.
The fine print. Revenue has fallen two straight quarters, the one profitable quarter was a paper gain, and a $520M impairment charge is disclosed but not yet booked.
A decent price for me: $38.47 or lower. Between my base and bull cases — that is where the risk of the transition and the size of the opportunity feel balanced.
